step1_analysis.circuit_type: Current Mode Logic (CML) Latch / Clocked Comparator
step1_analysis.description: A high-speed CML latch used as a quantizer in a continuous-time delta-sigma modulator. It consists of an input tracking pair and a cross-coupled latching pair sharing the same output nodes, driven by a clocked tail current steering mechanism and a cascode bias.

paper_reference.title: A 2-GHz Analog-to-Digital Delta-Sigma Modulator for CDMA Receivers With 79-dB Signal-to-Noise Ratio in 1.23-MHz Bandwidth

power_consumption.description: Average power consumption of the latch circuit

sky130_expected.calculation: Tail current I_tail ≈ 0.5 * u_n * C_ox * (W/L) * (V_bias - V_th)^2 = 0.5 * 270u * 10 * (0.9 - 0.42)^2 ≈ 311 uA. Power = I_tail * VDD = 311 uA * 1.8 V ≈ 0.56 mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on the 0.9V bias voltage and SKY130 NMOS parameters. The paper's 18mW is for the full ADC; a single CML latch consumes a small fraction of that.

clk_to_q_delay.description: Delay from the active clock edge to the differential output crossing zero

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the RC time constant at the output nodes. Assuming R_load = 1 kOhm and C_load ≈ 25 fF (parasitics for W=5u L=0.5u). tau = 25 ps. Delay is typically 2-3 tau ≈ 50-75 ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard delay for a CML latch in 130nm technology operating at 2 GHz. Must be significantly less than the 250ps half-period.

output_swing.description: Single-ended peak-to-peak voltage swing at the output nodes

sky130_expected.calculation: Swing = I_tail * R_load. With I_tail ≈ 311 uA and R_load = 1 kOhm, Swing ≈ 311 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: CML logic typically uses reduced swings (300-500mV) to maximize switching speed while keeping transistors in saturation.

operating_frequency.description: Maximum clock frequency at which the latch functions correctly

sky130_expected.calculation: f_max ≈ 1 / (4 * delay) ≈ 1 / 240ps ≈ 4 GHz. 2 GHz is well within the capability.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper specifies a 2 GHz sampling rate for the modulator. The testbench verifies operation at this frequency.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to verify latching function at 2 GHz, measure CLK-to-Q delay, output swing, and power consumption.
step3_testbench.spice:
* CML Latch Testbench
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u

* Supply and CML Load Resistors
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
R1 VDD OUTP 1k
R2 VDD OUTM 1k

* Bias Voltages
VLABEL_NET_3 LABEL_NET_3 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_4 LABEL_NET_4 0 0.9

* Differential Input (Toggles at 1 GHz, offset to change during hold phase)
VINP INP 0 PULSE(0.7 1.1 400p 20p 20p 480p 1000p)
VINM INM 0 PULSE(1.1 0.7 400p 20p 20p 480p 1000p)

* Differential Clock (2 GHz)
VCLK CLK 0 PULSE(0 1.8 0 20p 20p 230p 500p)
VCLKB CLKB 0 PULSE(1.8 0 0 20p 20p 230p 500p)

* DUT
XM1 OUTP OUTM N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 OUTP INM N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 OUTM OUTP N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 OUTM INP N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N1 CLKB N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N3 LABEL_NET_3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N0 LABEL_NET_4 N3 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N2 CLK N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
tran 2p 3n

* Calculate differential output
let vdiff = v(outp) - v(outm)

* Measure CLK-to-Q delay (from 2nd rising edge of CLK at 500ps to output crossing 0)
meas tran delay_clk_q trig v(clk) val=0.9 rise=2 targ vdiff val=0 rise=1

* Measure single-ended output swing
meas tran out_max max v(outp) from=1n to=3n
meas tran out_min min v(outp) from=1n to=3n
let swing = out_max - out_min
print swing

* Measure average power consumption
meas tran pwr_avg avg i(VVDD)
let power = -pwr_avg * 1.8
print power

quit
.endc
